display_input_power.note: GPU and display, keyboard, touch and switches, haptics, battery and charger, and USB gadget networking on a mainline phone. Instance: F(x)tec Pro1-X (SM6115): BOE BF060Y8M-AJ0 DSI panel, Adreno 610 under Mesa freedreno, Goodix touch, AW9523B-based sliding keyboard (driver from the NixOS port) with a hall slide switch and a GPIO keyboard LED, AW86224 haptics, PMI632 battery read by a board driver, a built-in USB CDC gadget. State as of 2026-10-27: display, GPU (GLES 3.2), touch with double-tap-to-wake, keyboard, slide switch, keyboard light, haptics and charging work on SailfishOS; GPU and memory throughput are below the hybris vendor stack; the panel logs a harmless backlight EINVAL; usb-moded cannot run beside the built-in gadget. SailfishOS daemon conventions (mce, ngfd) are in userspace_sailfishos.json.

display_gpu.title: Run the compositor on DRM/KMS with Mesa: eglfs_kms for Qt-based shells
display_gpu.general: A native port of a Qt-based phone shell runs its compositor on Qt eglfs with the KMS integration over Mesa GBM. Check that the Mesa build lists the GPU in its driver table before anything else. For SailfishOS lipstick: /var/lib/environment/compositor/*.conf with EGL_PLATFORM=drm, QT_QPA_PLATFORM=eglfs, QT_QPA_EGLFS_INTEGRATION=eglfs_kms, QT_QPA_EGLFS_KMS_CONFIG=/etc/eglfs-config.json (device /dev/dri/card0, hwcursor false) and the physical size, plus mesa (dri, EGL, GLESv2, gbm, wayland-egl), qt5-qtwayland-wayland_egl and qtscenegraph-adaptation from the shared native middleware repo.
display_gpu.instance: Pro1-X SailfishOS 5.1 on 7.1 (2026-10-23): native-common mesa 25.1.8 (libgallium) lists FD610 in its freedreno table; the Silica UI came up on the first successful boot with the config adapted from the PinePhone and victara ports (freedreno config credited to Mister_Magister's Moto X 2014 port); 68x136 mm physical size. Benchmark on 5.2: FD610 GLES 3.2.
display_gpu.source: port log 2026-10-23 10:22 (mesa rpm listing), 12:22 (Silica up); Pro1-X port repo port/droid-config-qx1050/sparse/var/lib/environment/compositor/droid-hal-device.conf; SailfishOS/devices.json fxtec_mainline_2026.sfos_on_mainline

display_gpu.title: Benchmark the mainline port against the vendor stack on the same SoC early
display_gpu.general: Run the same benchmark on the mainline port and on a vendor-kernel (hybris) port of the same device early: it separates CPU, memory, storage and GPU deficits. Expect GPU and memory throughput below the vendor stack in early freedreno bring-up. Check storage link speed and devfreq separately from file-path throughput.
display_gpu.instance: Pro1-X Benchymark 2.2.0, 2026-10-23 (mainline 7.1 freedreno against hybris 4.19 with the vendor blob, median of 4): CPU prime/single 0.99/0.98, memory 0.59, storage read/write 0.26/0.29, GPU stages 0.15-0.82 (Shader heavy 0.15, Cascade 0.26), Benchy small 1.42. UFS raw direct read 438 MB/s with UFS devfreq scaling 50 to 200 MHz under load, so the slow storage figure is the file/write path, not the link (confirmed). Low memory throughput suggests DDR/interconnect (bwmon) not scaling, and Shader heavy the ir3 compiler (both inferred). The UI feels 20-30 fps with occasional tearing; compositor-only gestures are smooth, transitions and lists stutter.
display_gpu.source: port log 'First Benchymark on mainline' 2026-10-23; moWerk 2026-10-23 19:10; Pro1-X port repo port/README.md

display_gpu.title: A DSI panel at 61 Hz instead of 60 can cause ghost touches
display_gpu.general: A pixel clock that drives the panel slightly above 60 Hz can produce touch ghost events; set the pixel clock for exactly 60 Hz.
display_gpu.instance: Pro1-X BOE BF060Y8M-AJ0: 165268 kHz gives 61.00 Hz, 162559 kHz gives 60 Hz (pro1x-dsi patch).

display_gpu.title: DCS backlight writes after blanking return EINVAL
display_gpu.general: A DSI panel with DCS backlight control can reject brightness writes while the panel is blanked ('Failed to write display brightness: -22' in the kernel log, EINVAL to userspace). It is harmless log noise, but a display daemon that fades the backlight around blanking may show a visible jump.
display_gpu.instance: Pro1-X BOE bf060y8m on 7.1 and 7.3: once in hours of uptime in the kernel log; SailfishOS mce (1.116.5) logs 'can't flush .../brightness' for /sys/class/backlight/5e94000.dsi.0/brightness, and the dim fade jumps to full brightness once per power-key press. Open.
display_gpu.source: SailfishOS/mainline_porting.json mce.backlight_write_einval; moWerk 2026-10-23 19:46; Pro1-X port repo port/notes/upstream.md

display_gpu.title: Generate DSI panel drivers from the downstream DT
display_gpu.general: Extract the DTB from the stock boot image and generate the mainline DRM panel driver with linux-mdss-dsi-panel-driver-generator instead of hand-porting init sequences; verify the output, since wrong init commands can leave the panel dark, and keep simple-framebuffer as the fallback until the DSI driver works. Phones are often multi-sourced for panels and touch: detect the variant in the bootloader and patch the DT rather than in the kernel.
display_gpu.instance: General guidance; the Pro1-X panel driver (boe,bf060y8m-aj0) has been upstream since v5.17.

input.title: Capture the mainline keyboard's keycodes before reusing an old layout
input.general: xkb layouts written for a vendor kernel driver may assume different keycodes. Capture the mainline driver's codes with a key monitor (keyd monitor, evtest) while someone presses each keycap, then decide which layout fits.
input.instance: Pro1-X mainline pro1x-keyboard driver, 2026-10-23: with stock xkb de(nodeadkeys) every QWERTZ letter key is right (u-umlaut on [, + on ], o-umlaut on ;, a-umlaut on ', < on 102nd, y/z swapped as expected). The 2019/2020 xkeyboard-config-pro1 for the hybris Pro1 used shifted codes and is not reusable as-is; the Pro1-X QWERTZ Fn legends also differ from the Pro1 table.

input.title: Report a dedicated Fn key as RIGHTALT and put its legends on xkb level 3
input.general: xkb only handles keycodes up to 255, so a Fn key reported as KEY_FN (464) cannot be a level modifier; Qt's built-in evdev keyboard handler (used without libinput) drops scancodes missing from its keymap entirely. Map the Fn key to KEY_RIGHTALT in the DT keymap and put the Fn legends on level 3 in one xkb symbols file selected by the shell's layout setting, instead of forking xkeyboard-config. Validate the symbols on the host with xkbcli compile-keymap. Because this remap serves one OS's input stack, keep it out of upstream DT.
input.instance: Pro1-X: two yellow Fn keys are gpio-keys with KEY_FN; the SailfishOS-only DT patch maps them to KEY_RIGHTALT; symbols fxtec_vndr/pro1x (includes de(nodeadkeys), level 3 = Fn legends) selected through lipstick dconf /desktop/lipstick-jolla-home/layout and variant (alternative: a custom qmap through LIPSTICK_OPTIONS). The hybris Pro1 used RIGHTALT the same way (level3(ralt_switch)).
input.source: xkbcli validation 2026-10-23 21:41-21:43; Pro1-X port repo port/notes/research/research-keyboard.md, port/README.md

input.title: Keyboard LED polarity: check the trigger logic at rest before flipping a GPIO
input.general: When an LED appears inverted, first check the trigger logic at rest (switch semantics, daemon policy, UI state) before flipping the LED GPIO polarity; two inversions can cancel out or double up. Separate the real DT bug from OS workarounds once found.
input.instance: Pro1-X keyboard backlight on tlmm 103: on NixOS writing 1 to /sys/class/leds/white:kbd_backlight lit it with the stock DT (2026-10-23); after a 'reversed' report the SailfishOS DT flipped it to ACTIVE_LOW, and later the real inversion was found in the slide-switch semantics, which left doubt whether the LED flip was right. The kernel handover of 2026-10-26 classifies the LED as active-low, a real and upstreamable DT bug, unlike the slide inversion and the Fn remap.
input.source: port log 2026-10-23 01:22, 21:01, 23:47; Pro1-X port repo port/kernel/HANDOVER.md, port/notes/upstream.md

input.title: Test wake gestures early
input.general: Mainline touch drivers may support wake gestures such as double-tap-to-wake without vendor userspace; test them on the first UI boot.
input.instance: Pro1-X SailfishOS on 7.1 (2026-10-23): double-tap-to-wake worked reliably (three times in a row), unexpectedly; it does not on the Jolla C2 hybris port.

haptics.title: An accepted FF_RUMBLE can still be unfelt: motor strength is a driver parameter
haptics.general: A force-feedback play the kernel accepts can still be too weak to feel; the motor driver's module parameters (gain, drive level) decide. Test the motor with a direct EVIOCSFF upload from a small static tool before blaming the OS's feedback stack, and ship the working values as a modprobe.d option.
haptics.instance: Pro1-X AW86224 (mainline-style driver, FF_RUMBLE only, 16 memless slots): driver defaults gain 6 / drive 59 not felt; d2s_gain=7 drv2_lvl=100 felt (stronger warms the motor); /etc/modprobe.d/aw86224.conf; tested with a static musl ffrumble tool, 2026-10-23.
haptics.source: SailfishOS/mainline_porting.json vibration_ngfd.strength; port log 2026-10-23 21:00-21:05; Pro1-X port repo port/droid-config-qx1050/sparse/etc/modprobe.d/aw86224.conf

power.title: Battery and charger need their own drivers; a board-specific estimator is not an upstream route
power.general: Battery level and charging need drivers in the device series, and they must survive any derived kernel config (see the lost-option guard in kernel.json). Where the PMIC fuel-gauge path is not supported upstream, a board driver estimating the level from PMIC ADC readings plus a charger input-limit/watchdog driver works, but the real upstream path is the PMIC's ADC and fuel-gauge support.
power.instance: Pro1-X PMI632: pro1x-power (+897 lines: pro1x-adc-battery, pro1x-icl); battery 99 % and charging read correctly; the first SailfishOS-derived config lost the battery-level driver (2026-10-23).
power.source: port log 2026-10-23 13:16, 16:05; Pro1-X port repo port/kernel/HANDOVER.md

usb.title: A built-in CDC composite gadget gives ssh from the first boot, but blocks the OS's USB mode daemon
usb.general: A precomposed gadget built into the kernel (CONFIG_USB_CDC_COMPOSITE=y: serial ttyGS0 plus ECM usb0, fixed MACs) gives network and serial for any OS on the device, and IPv6 link-local ssh works before any DHCP. Give usb0 a static address (busybox udhcpd for clients) and open INPUT on it: a firewall that drops traffic on interfaces it does not manage (SailfishOS connman sets INPUT DROP) makes the gadget unreachable otherwise. The price: the OS's own USB mode daemon (usb-moded on SailfishOS: MTP, the mode menu) cannot run, and units that wait for it fail (policies-setup.service). Keep it during bring-up and turn the option off in the release kernel.
usb.instance: Pro1-X 7.1/7.3: g_cdc built in, usb0 at 172.16.42.1 with clients .11-.20 (the NixOS gadget default), qx1050-usb-net.service; the phone showed the address but the host could not ping until qx1050-usb-net.sh accepted usb0, then ping6 0.6 ms; the link-local address answers under NixOS and SailfishOS with different host keys; no UI reaction to USB plug on SailfishOS.
usb.source: port log 2026-10-23 10:26, 12:48-12:55, 13:54; Pro1-X port repo port/droid-config-qx1050/sparse/usr/bin/droid/qx1050-usb-net.sh, port/kernel/pro1x.fragment, port/notes/sfos-5.2-upgrade.md

usb.title: Put the kernel console on the USB serial gadget
usb.general: With a serial gadget, add console=ttyGS0 to the command line so early boot can be read on the host (/dev/ttyACM*) when the display is useless.
usb.instance: Pro1-X NixOS command line carries console=ttyGS0; in this period the USB network came up during a UI hang and was used instead, so the serial console itself was not exercised.
